name: Nonogram Puzzle
description: Black-and-white nonogram: deduce filled cells from row/column clues; puzzles are generated locally and verified to have a unique solution
help: Offers 5×5, 10×10 and 15×15 boards. Each new puzzle is extracted from an original random pattern in Rust, then independently solved to verify uniqueness — ambiguous or unsolvable candidates are discarded, never delivered.
Left-click or drag to fill black, right-click or drag to mark empty; drags only affect undetermined cells and count as one undo step; arrow keys move, space fills, enter marks empty.
Clue completion marks and conflict highlights update only on an explicit “Check”; undetermined cells are never treated as confirmed empty. Solving requires every row and column to match.

The “Hint” uses single-line candidate-overlap reasoning and fills one cell, stating which row/column it came from; when no such inference exists it says so plainly instead of secretly inserting answers.

Export a printable file with the puzzle page and a separate solution page (HTML; print in a browser). Hint/solution usage is recorded honestly. All puzzles are self-generated — no commercial puzzle packs.

check.won: Solved! Every row and column matches its clues.

hint.none: No cell can be determined by single-line inference on the current board; deeper branching is beyond the first-version hint.

paper.title: Puzzle paper
paper.hint: Export HTML and print in a browser; page 1 is the puzzle, page 2 the solution.

errors.puz.solution_size: Solution length does not match the board
